title: Sliding-window affinity eviction with snapshot-fencing for KV shards
creator: Lena Ortiz
body:
Background:
We operate a GPU-backed KV cache keyed by model prefix tokens to accelerate continuous batching and autoregressive generation. Existing eviction strategies (pure LRU, TTL, or simple prefix trimming) either starve long-running prompts, cause prefix-coherence violations under batching, or lead to frequent GPU OOMs under transient load spikes.

Goal:
Design and implement a hybrid eviction policy that:
- Maintains strong correctness guarantees (no stale prefix reads, safe in-flight reference semantics)
- Preserves prefix affinity where beneficial for latency and KV reuse
- Smooths memory usage during bursts and avoids catastrophic OOMs
- Integrates with continuous batching without blocking tail-latency SLOs

Proposal summary (Sliding-window affinity + Snapshot Fencing):
1) Sliding-window affinity score: each prefix shard maintains a time-decayed access score (leaky-window counter) that blends recency (LRU-like) and frequency (LFU-like) while exposing a TTL component. The decay half-life is configurable per workload profile.
2) Soft/Hard watermarks per GPU slab: memory reclamation uses two thresholds. On crossing soft watermark, low-affinity slots are marked reclaimable; on hard watermark we aggressively evict according to a prioritized eviction queue.
3) Snapshot-fencing for in-flight batches: when a request begins using a KV prefix, it obtains a transient fence token (epoch id + sequence). Fenced slots are immortal to eviction until the fence is released or a grace timeout elapses. This prevents prefix coherence regressions during continuous batching when multiple micro-batches may reference the same KV.
4) Prefetch and pin hints: scheduler and batcher can pass affinity hints (next-token prefetch probability) to increase a prefix's score temporarily, reducing evictions for likely-reused contexts.
5) Graceful demotion and compact-on-evict: evicted entries go through a demotion window where compressed or quantized representations can be stored in pinned host memory or on-device lower-precision slabs rather than being fully dropped, preserving partial reuse for heavy tails.

Correctness invariants and rationale:
- Linearizability for GET/PUT/UNPIN: every GET/PUT must observe a consistent snapshot w.r.t fences. Fencing ensures that an in-progress generation cannot observe evicted KV slices mid-request.
- Safe eviction never reclaims a slot with active fence tokens. A fence token is released deterministically on batch completion or forcibly after a bounded grace timeout (configurable).
- No prefix split-read: when prefix re-chaining occurs due to eviction+reconstruction, callers see either the old contiguous KV or the fully rebuilt KV; there is no hybrid state. This is achieved via an atomic pointer-swap at reconstruct time guarded by fence epochs.

Design details and data structures:
- Affinity counter: 64-bit float decay counter per prefix-shard. Updates are lock-free increments on access; periodic background decay applied per epoch.
- Eviction queue: a priority heap of (affinity_score, last_access_ts, tenant_weight, size_bytes). Tie-breaks favor smaller slots to reduce fragmentation.
- Fence table: compact per-GPU table mapping fence_token -> list of pinned slot ids and epoch. Fence entries are reference-counted.
- Demotion store: compressed representation kept in host or lower-precision slabs with a fast rehydrate path when reclamation happens.

Testing and validation plan:
- Property-based fuzzing harness (kv-fuzz) that injects concurrent GET/PUT, forced fence timeouts, and artificial GPU OOM signals. Assert invariants: no stale reads, no double-free, and memory accounting correctness.
- Simulation environment: extend the eviction-emulator to model sliding-window decay and fence latencies; run workload traces from production (chat-heavy and embedding-heavy) for 72h each to measure evictions and reconstructed KV rates.
- Microbench: benchmark with continuous batching harness to measure P50/P95 latency and tokens/sec before/after. Target: P95 increase <5% under same throughput, reconstruction rate <0.5% of accesses.
- Safety fuzz runs integrated in CI: daily smoke tests that force hard watermark and validate graceful degradation policies and rollback.

Implementation status and progress updates:
- 2026-02-18: RFC posted to team (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/Sliding-Window-Affinity-RFC).
- 2026-02-24: Prototype of affinity counters and eviction queue implemented in rust/core-kv (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core-kv/pull/912).
- 2026-03-01: Snapshot-fencing API landed (internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1043). Basic fence table implemented; unit tests added.
- 2026-03-07: Demotion store completed and host-resident compressed format defined (doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/file/demotion-format-v1).
- 2026-03-09: Simulation runs completed on prod traces. Key results: 32% fewer full reconstructs vs LRU baseline, 12% lower P50 latency under burst; worst-case P95 increase 4.2%. Attached simulation artifacts in artifacts/ENG-812479/sim-results-20260309.tar.gz.
- 2026-03-10: PR open for integration tests and CI (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1070) — currently awaiting review from infra and runtime owners.

Code review feedback (high level):
- Request to add stronger invariants in runtime panics when fence refcount mismatches detected (addressed in PR#1070).
- Concern about fence grace-timeout interacting with distributed preemption — added a safety check to defer forced eviction until fence epoch advanced.

Risks and open questions:
- Long-lived fences under slow downstream clients can pin significant memory. Mitigation: add adaptive grace-timeout that drops with global memory pressure and informs caller via a deterministic error path.
- Quantized demotion rehydrate latency might hurt tail latency for some workloads. We'll gate quantized demotion by per-tenant QoS tiers.
- Cross-GPU reconstruction cost when sharded KV gets evicted on one GPU but partially present on another. Plan: prefer co-locating shard affinity and include heuristics to avoid cross-GPU fragmentation.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on internal non-prod cluster with hard watermark set conservative (lower eviction aggressiveness). Monitor reconstruct rate, latency, OOMs for 48h.
2) Gradual ramp to production with per-tenant control: start with low-traffic tenants and Dedicated customers.
3) Enable demotion store incrementally behind runtime flag.
4) Full fleet rollout with monitoring alerts and automatic rollback on safety violations.

Next steps (short-term):
- Address Infra review comments and merge PR#1070 (owner: Marco).
- Add adaptive grace-timeout heuristics and expose metric for pinned-by-fence bytes.
- Add a small runtime migration job to compute initial affinity scores from historical traces for warm startups.
